title: PTI protest march and emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated to demand the release of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan and voiced grievances over harsh economic conditions.
tea.want: Release of the jailed former prime minister and anti-government demands.
tea.changed: Oct 12: Pakistani authorities detained 278 party members following emergency rule.

summary: Supporters of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), the opposition party of former Prime Minister Imran Khan, held a large protest march in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, including Peshawar, demanding the release of the jailed former leader and protesting against harsh economic conditions. The demonstrations prompted the central government to suspend the PTI-led provincial government and impose emergency rule on Sunday, citing the party's failure to tackle terrorism and deteriorating security. In response to the emergency measures and ongoing unrest, authorities deployed heavy police forces, set up makeshift barriers using shipping containers and razor wire, closed schools, and caused internet disruptions. Police officials reported detaining hundreds of party members following the declaration.
demands: Release of the jailed former prime minister
response: According to police officials and federal ministers, authorities imposed emergency rule, disbanded the provincial government citing security and terrorism concerns, deployed large numbers of police personnel with riot gear, blocked roads with containers, and detained 278 PTI members.

arrests.text: 278 PTI members had been detained in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province since the emergency declaration

updates.text: Pakistan suspended the provincial government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid large protest marches led by PTI.
Police officials reported detaining 278 PTI members following the imposition of emergency rule.
